title: Outside the Chancery
sceneText:
The last market day of October. The square is thinner than last time, but there are people on the chancery street.

Two men come out of the chancery door. One in dark grey uniform, one in a dark green coat. The green coat has an earthenware bottle in his hand and is talking, quickly; the grey uniform walks beside him at about half a step, saying nothing, and not walking any faster either.

They stop at the corner. Thierry holds the bottle out towards Timothy. Timothy looks at the bottle for two seconds, and then takes it. He takes it naturally enough, but those two seconds were real.

He drinks a mouthful and hands it back.

They see you at the same moment.

Thierry waves first. “Steward. Selling today?”

Timothy gives you a nod and moves the bottle to his other hand.

choices.text: Ask Timothy about Millridge’s felling declarations

effects.logEntry: You asked Timothy about Millridge’s felling declarations.

choices.resultText:
Thierry says easily that he will go and look at something else, and walks off.

Timothy does not move.

You ask him about the felling declarations from Millridge.

“I cannot show you another party’s file,” he says. And then he pauses.

“But the duchy’s table of allowances is public. It is posted on the board over there. You can read it yourself.” He points towards the north end. “Millridge declared a total of forty this year, with a diameter limit of thirty.”

“The oak that actually went out of the north district this year — I signed the loading records at the wharf myself. What went out from Millridge was fifty-two.”

Having said those two numbers, he stops.

“A difference of twelve units,” you say.

“A difference of twelve units.” He repeats it. “Spread over three years that is four units a year, and four units a year across a forestry district of five thousand hectares is inside the margin of measurement error. Which is why it is not worth opening a case on.”

He lifts the bottle in his hand and looks at it; he has probably not yet decided whether to carry the thing back with him.

“Baron von Alder’s previous steward asked me the same question three years ago.”

choices.text: Show Thierry the cloth bundle Gregor gave you

effects.logEntry: You spread out Gregor’s cloth bundle in front of Thierry.

choices.resultText:
Timothy says he has something else to deliver, and goes.

You take out the cloth bundle Gregor gave you.

Thierry finds a stone ledge at the side of the street, opens the bundle out and works the dried stuff apart with two fingers. He looks at it a long time. Much longer than you expected.

“This is wrong,” he says.

You ask what is wrong.

“This time of year, this should not be anywhere around here.” He picks up a very fine stem. “It grows where there is water, and it wants shade, and it wants cool. The low bottoms are too warm; this would not live down there into October.”

He looks up at the line of the hills to the north.

“Higher up. A hollow up high with water in it and out of the sun. Beyond my line, I can think of three.”

He wraps the bundle up again and hands it back to you.

“The mud?” he asks.

You say it was black, and it had a smell.

“Then it is two,” he says. “One of the three has a stone bottom. No black mud out of that.”

He draws two points on the stone ledge with a finger, about an inch apart.

“Those two places are a full day’s walk. If you want to go, tell me and I will take you. You will not find them alone. There is no path in.”
